findings.risk: A <button> without a type attribute defaults to type="submit" in most browsers. Inside a form, this causes the button to submit the form when clicked, even if its purpose is something else (e.g. open a modal, toggle a menu). This leads to accidental form submissions that are hard to debug.
findings.solution: Always specify the type attribute. Use type="button" for buttons that trigger actions, type="submit" for form submission buttons, and type="reset" for form reset buttons.
findings.benefit: Explicit, predictable button behavior — no accidental form submissions, clear intent for every button in the codebase.

findings.risk: A <button> without a type attribute defaults to type="submit" in most browsers. Inside a form, this causes the button to submit the form when clicked, even if its purpose is something else (e.g. open a modal, toggle a menu). This leads to accidental form submissions that are hard to debug.
findings.solution: Always specify the type attribute. Use type="button" for buttons that trigger actions, type="submit" for form submission buttons, and type="reset" for form reset buttons.
findings.benefit: Explicit, predictable button behavior — no accidental form submissions, clear intent for every button in the codebase.

findings.risk: Links with target="_blank" without rel="noopener noreferrer" allow the newly opened page to access the opener window via window.opener. This creates a security vulnerability (reverse tabnapping) and a privacy leak (the referrer URL is sent to the target site).
findings.solution: Always add rel="noopener noreferrer" to every link with target="_blank". Modern browsers apply noopener automatically, but the explicit declaration ensures compatibility and prevents referrer leaks.
findings.benefit: Prevents reverse tabnapping attacks and referrer leaks — third-party sites opened in new tabs cannot manipulate the original page.

findings.risk: Without a viewport meta tag, mobile browsers render the page at desktop width and then scale it down, making text and UI elements unreadably small. The page is effectively unusable on mobile devices without pinch-to-zoom.
findings.solution: Add <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"> in the <head> section. Do not add user-scalable=no (see WCAG 1.4.4).
findings.benefit: Responsive design foundation — the page adapts to the device screen width, providing a usable experience on all screen sizes without horizontal scrolling.

findings.risk: Links with target="_blank" without rel="noopener noreferrer" allow the newly opened page to access the opener window via window.opener. This creates a security vulnerability (reverse tabnapping) and a privacy leak (the referrer URL is sent to the target site).
findings.solution: Always add rel="noopener noreferrer" to every link with target="_blank". Modern browsers apply noopener automatically, but the explicit declaration ensures compatibility and prevents referrer leaks.
findings.benefit: Prevents reverse tabnapping attacks and referrer leaks — third-party sites opened in new tabs cannot manipulate the original page.

Inside a form, this causes the button to submit the form when clicked, even if its purpose is something else (e.g. open a modal, toggle a menu). findings.solution: Always specify the type attribute. Use type="button" for buttons that trigger actions, type="submit" for form submission buttons, and type="reset" for form reset buttons.
findings.benefit: Explicit, predictable button behavior — no accidental form submissions, clear intent for every button in the codebase.

findings.risk: A page without a main landmark (<main> or role="main") forces screen reader users to navigate through all content without a shortcut to the primary content, significantly increasing cognitive load.
findings.solution: Wrap the primary page content in a <main> element. Only one <main> per page.
findings.benefit: Compliance with WCAG 1.3.6 and 2.4.1 — Bypass Blocks — users can jump directly to the main content.

findings.risk: A table header cell without a scope attribute leaves screen readers unable to determine which data cells it applies to, making complex tables inaccessible.
findings.solution: Add scope="col" for column headers or scope="row" for row headers on every <th> element.
findings.benefit: Compliance with WCAG 1.3.1 — Info and Relationships — table structure is programmatically determinable by assistive technologies.

findings.risk: A page without a main landmark (<main> or role="main") forces screen reader users to navigate through all content without a shortcut to the primary content, significantly increasing cognitive load.
findings.solution: Wrap the primary page content in a <main> element. Only one <main> per page.
findings.benefit: Compliance with WCAG 1.3.6 and 2.4.1 — Bypass Blocks — users can jump directly to the main content.

findings.solution: Add scope="col" for column headers or scope="row" for row headers on every <th> element.
findings.benefit: Compliance with WCAG 1.3.1 — Info and Relationships — table structure is programmatically determinable by assistive technologies.

findings.risk: A page without a main landmark (<main> or role="main") forces screen reader users to navigate through all content without a shortcut to the primary content, significantly increasing cognitive load.
findings.solution: Wrap the primary page content in a <main> element. Only one <main> per page.
findings.benefit: Compliance with WCAG 1.3.6 and 2.4.1 — Bypass Blocks — users can jump directly to the main content.

findings.risk: A page without a main landmark (<main> or role="main") forces screen reader users to navigate through all content without a shortcut to the primary content, significantly increasing cognitive load.
findings.solution: Wrap the primary page content in a <main> element. Only one <main> per page.
findings.benefit: Compliance with WCAG 1.3.6 and 2.4.1 — Bypass Blocks — users can jump directly to the main content.

findings.risk: A table header cell without a scope attribute leaves screen readers unable to determine which data cells it applies to, making complex tables inaccessible.
findings.solution: Add scope="col" for column headers or scope="row" for row headers on every <th> element.
findings.benefit: Compliance with WCAG 1.3.1 — Info and Relationships — table structure is programmatically determinable by assistive technologies.

findings.risk: A page without a main landmark (<main> or role="main") forces screen reader users to navigate through all content without a shortcut to the primary content, significantly increasing cognitive load.
findings.solution: Wrap the primary page content in a <main> element. Only one <main> per page.
findings.benefit: Compliance with WCAG 1.3.6 and 2.4.1 — Bypass Blocks — users can jump directly to the main content.

findings.risk: A table header cell without a scope attribute leaves screen readers unable to determine which data cells it applies to, making complex tables inaccessible.
findings.solution: Add scope="col" for column headers or scope="row" for row headers on every <th> element.
findings.benefit: Compliance with WCAG 1.3.1 — Info and Relationships — table structure is programmatically determinable by assistive technologies.

findings.benefit: Precise exception handling — only expected errors are caught, unexpected failures propagate correctly and are visible in logs.
